title: Optimizing Docker images
idea: Fast, small images need three habits: order layers by change rate, exclude unneeded files with `.dockerignore`, and start from a small base image.
points: Docker rebuilds a layer when its inputs change, and every layer after it.
The build context is the folder you send to Docker; `.dockerignore` trims it.
Ignored files cannot trigger a rebuild or reach the image through `COPY`.
Small bases (`-alpine`, `-slim`) mean less to download and store.

steps.caption: The first build has an empty cache, so every line runs.
Edit `src/routes.js`. Only `COPY . .` depends on it, so the install is not repeated.
Edit `README.md`, which `.dockerignore` lists. Docker never sees the change, so every layer comes from cache.
Add a dependency. `package.json` is copied above the install, so the slow layer runs again.

code.title: .dockerignore
code.caption: Save it as `.dockerignore` in the root of the build context, next to the Dockerfile.

walk.text: Your laptop's packages. The image runs its own `npm ci`.
Git history is large and never needed at runtime.
Secrets must never be copied into an image layer.
Log files in any folder. `**/` matches any depth; plain `*.log` matches only the root.
Docs the app does not need. Editing them no longer touches the cache.

code.title: Watch the cache
code.caption: The second build reuses the install layer. `--no-cache` ignores the cache and runs every line.

pitfalls: List `.env` in `.dockerignore`; otherwise `COPY . .` bakes your secrets into the image.
Test before switching to Alpine: its C library differs, and some native packages break.
Avoid `latest` as a base: tags move, so two builds can differ.

quiz.q: Which change makes the npm ci layer run again on the next build?
quiz.why: `COPY package*.json` copies the lockfile, so changing it invalidates that layer and every layer after it, including the install.

takeaway: For each line and file ask: does it change often, and must it ship?

starters: What exactly goes into the build context?
